mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% year-over-year signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to monetary tightening, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPI YoY > 2%.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% signals a tightening labor market, which increases wage pressures and reduces corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Real Final Sales (RSAFS) above a 3% quarter-over-quarter growth rate signals strong consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances where RSAFS QoQ > 3%.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in Industrial Production (INDPRO) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a contraction in supply, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced economic activity.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO MoM < -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 25 basis points in a single meeting signals a hawkish monetary policy stance, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate higher borrowing costs.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS increases > 0.25%.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in Nonfarm Payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances where PAYEMS increases > 200k.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in Housing Starts (HOUST) and Real Final Sales (RSAFS) signals a broad-based increase in demand, which boosts corporate earnings and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances where both HOUST and RSAFS increase.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle, a decrease in GDP (GDPC1) growth rate below 1% quarter-over-quarter signals a weakening economy, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances during a tightening cycle where GDPC1 QoQ < 1%.
